The paper investigates the application of chiral layers and metamaterials as radar absorbing materials for reducing radar cross section (RCS).
Chiral media exhibit magneto-electric coupling, leading to properties such as optical activity, circular dichroism, and polarization transformation.
Chiral nihility is a special case of chiral media where both permittivity and permeability are simultaneously zero.
The paper analyzes the reflection properties of a PEC plate coated with chiral layers under various conditions, including nondispersive, dispersive, and chiral nihility.
The Genetic Algorithm (GA) method is used to optimize the chiral coatings for minimizing reflected power from a PEC plane in a specified frequency bandwidth and range of incident angles.
Key parameters optimized include relative permittivity, relative permeability, chirality parameter, thickness of the chiral layer, and the distance between the chiral layer and the PEC plane.
The designed absorber achieves low reflection for both TE and TM polarizations in a wide frequency bandwidth (8–12 GHz) and wide angles of incidence.
Optimized parameters for the nondispersive chiral nihility absorber: εr = -j0.180, µr = -j0.201, κ = 1.431 - 0.008j, d = 1.6 mm, t = 8.1 mm.
At normal incidence, the dispersive chiral absorber achieves two perfect absorptivity peaks at 9 GHz and 11 GHz, with absorptivity ratios up to 99%.
With increasing angle of incidence, the absorption for both TE and TM polarizations remains up to 90%.

The CMM structure is periodic in the x-y plane, with a unit cell consisting of two copper double arms conjugated gammadion patterned on opposite sides of an FR-4 board with dielectric constant 4.2 and loss tangent 0.02.
Geometric parameters of the CMM unit cell: a = 10 mm, L = 3.45 mm, l1 = 4.05 mm, l2 = 4.95 mm, w = s = 0.3 mm, d = 1.6 mm.
At normal incidence, the CMM structure shows two perfect absorptivity peaks at 6.3 GHz and 6.9 GHz, with absorptivity ratios up to 99%.
The absorber structure is almost polarization insensitive, with absorptivity peaks remaining almost unchanged for different polarization angles.
The genetic algorithm is used to optimize the chiral coatings for minimizing reflected power, allowing for the design of wideband and angle-insensitive microwave absorbers.
The paper concludes that dispersive chiral layers and metamaterials are suitable for the application of absorbers.
Multi-layer chiral metamaterials can be optimally designed as wideband microwave absorbers in the future.
